content.text:
Here is a basic diagram of an Ecommerce Application Architecture:

- The User accesses the site via a Web Browser.
- Requests go to a Load Balancer (Entry Point), which routes to the Django App Server (Ecommerce API).
- The App queries a PostgreSQL Database (for Orders and Products).
- Static files (like images) are served from Object Storage.
- Payment requests are processed via Stripe (Payments).

Would you like to see additional details (e.g., for order fulfillment or inventory systems) or a different style (e.g., Mermaid code for editable diagrams)?

Create a comprehensive system architecture diagram for a real-time global e-commerce platform. The diagram should show the full request lifecycle from user device to data layer and back.
Include the following layers and components:
Client Layer: Mobile app (iOS/Android), Web browser (React SPA), and a Smart TV app — all connecting through a global CDN with edge caching nodes in North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific.
API Gateway Layer: Show a load balancer routing to an API Gateway cluster, which fans out to: an Auth Service (JWT + OAuth2), a Rate Limiter, and a GraphQL Federation Gateway that aggregates multiple downstream microservices.
Microservices Layer (10+ services): Product Catalog, Inventory, Pricing Engine, User Profile, Cart & Checkout, Order Management, Recommendation Engine (ML-based), Fraud Detection, Notification Service (email/push/SMS), and a Search Service backed by Elasticsearch.
Async Communication: Show a central Kafka event bus with named topics (order.created, inventory.updated, fraud.flagged) connecting services that publish and subscribe. Include a dead-letter queue for failed messages.
Data Layer: Each microservice has its own database (polyglot persistence) — show PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis (for caching and sessions), Cassandra (for time-series order history), and S3 (for product images/assets).
Observability Stack: Show a side-panel with Prometheus scraping all services, feeding into Grafana dashboards, with logs going to an ELK Stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana), and distributed tracing via Jaeger.
CI/CD Pipeline: Illustrate a GitHub Actions pipeline flowing into Docker image builds → ECR registry → Helm chart deployments → Kubernetes cluster (EKS) across 3 availability zones, with ArgoCD for GitOps.
Use color-coding by layer, dashed lines for async flows, solid lines for synchronous HTTP/gRPC calls, and add latency annotations (e.g., “~12ms”, “~200ms”) on critical paths. Mark failure points with a warning icon and include a legend.

args.code:
# Legend (not a node, for visualization reference only):
# Solid Edge = Sync HTTP/gRPC (~12-200ms)
# Dashed Edge = Async Event (Kafka)
# Warning Icon = Failure point

# CLIENT LAYER
user = User("User")
mobile = Mobile("Mobile App\n(iOS/Android)")
web = React("React SPA\n(Web)")
tv = Client("Smart TV App")
cdn_na = Cloudflare("CDN\n(N. America)")
cdn_eu = Cloudflare("CDN\n(Europe)")
cdn_apac = Cloudflare("CDN\n(Asia-Pacific)")
user >> [mobile, web, tv]
[mobile, web, tv] >> [cdn_na, cdn_eu, cdn_apac]
# API LAYER
lb = Nginx("Load Balancer")
api_gw = APIGateway("API Gateway\n(Cluster)")
lb >> Edge(label="Routes\n~18ms") >> api_gw
api_gw >> Edge(label="Routes\n~9ms") >> [cdn_na, cdn_eu, cdn_apac]
api_gw >> Edge(label="Sync\nCalls") >> ["Auth Service", "Rate Limiter", "GraphQL Gateway"]
auth = GcpIAM("Auth Service\n(JWT+OAuth2)")
rate = Server("Rate Limiter")
gql = GraphQL("GraphQL\nFederation GW")
api_gw >> Edge(label="Authorize\n~12ms") >> auth
api_gw >> Edge(label="Limit reqs") >> rate
api_gw >> Edge(label="Fan-out\n~20ms") >> gql

# MICROSERVICES LAYER
with Cluster("Microservices"):
    catalog = Server("Product Catalog")
    inventory = Server("Inventory")
    pricing = Server("Pricing Engine")
    profile = Server("User Profile")
    cart = Server("Cart & Checkout")
    order = Server("Order Mgmt")
    reco = VertexAI("Recs Engine\n(ML Based)")
    fraud = Server("Fraud Detect")
    notif = Server("Notification\n(Email/SMS/Push)")
    search = ElasticSearch("Search\nService")

    # GraphQL to all services
    gql >> Edge(label="HTTP/gRPC\n~20-80ms") >> [catalog, inventory, pricing, profile, cart, order, reco, fraud, notif, search]

    # Kafka Event Bus
    kafka = Kafka("Kafka Event Bus")
    kafka_topics = [
        Kafka("Topic: order.created"),
        Kafka("Topic: inventory.updated"),
        Kafka("Topic: fraud.flagged")
    ]
    kafka >> kafka_topics
    # Event publishing
    order >> Edge(style="dashed", label="Publishes (order.created)") >> kafka_topics[0]
    inventory >> Edge(style="dashed", label="Publishes (inventory.updated)") >> kafka_topics[1]
    fraud >> Edge(style="dashed", label="Publishes (fraud.flagged)") >> kafka_topics[2]
    # Event subscriptions
    reco >> Edge(style="dashed", label="Subscribes (order.created)") >> kafka_topics[0]
    notif >> Edge(style="dashed", label="Subscribes all") >> kafka_topics
    cart >> Edge(style="dashed", label="Subscribes (inventory.updated)") >> kafka_topics[1]
    # Dead-letter queue
    dlq = Kafka("DLQ (Failed Msg)")
    kafka_topics >> Edge(style="dashed", label="Fails to") >> dlq

# DATA LAYER (Polyglot persistence) - Each svc owns DB
with Cluster("Databases"):
    db_catalog = PostgreSQL("Catalog DB\n(PostgreSQL)")
    db_inventory = MongoDB("Inventory DB\n(MongoDB)")
    db_pricing = Redis("Pricing Cache\n(Redis)")
    db_profile = PostgreSQL("Profile DB\n(PostgreSQL)")
    db_cart = Redis("Cart DB\n(Redis)")
    db_order = Cassandra("Order Hist\n(Cassandra)")
    db_reco = PostgreSQL("Reco ML DB")
    db_fraud = PostgreSQL("Fraud DB")
    db_search = ElasticSearch("Search IDX\n(ElasticSearch)")
    assets = Storage("S3\n(Product Images)")
    # Wiring svc to DB
    catalog >> Edge(label="Queries/Updates") >> db_catalog
    inventory >> Edge(label="Queries/Updates") >> db_inventory
    pricing >> Edge(label="Caches/Reads") >> db_pricing
    profile >> Edge(label="Queries/Updates") >> db_profile
    cart >> Edge(label="Reads/Updates") >> db_cart
    order >> Edge(label="Queries/Updates") >> db_order
    reco >> Edge(label="Reads/Writes") >> db_reco
    fraud >> Edge(label="Queries/Updates") >> db_fraud
    search >> Edge(label="Indexes/Queries") >> db_search
    catalog >> Edge(label="Stores images") >> assets

# Observability (side-panel)
with Cluster("Observability"):
    prom = Prometheus("Prometheus")
    grafana = Grafana("Grafana Dashboard")
    elk = Elastic("ELK Stack\n(Logs)")
    jaeger = Jaeger("Jaeger Tracing")
    [prom, elk, jaeger] >> Edge(label="Scrape/Log/Trace") >> [catalog, inventory, pricing, profile, cart, order, reco, fraud, notif, search]
    prom >> Edge(label="Feeds") >> grafana

# CI/CD PIPELINE
with Cluster("CI/CD Pipeline"):
    github = GithubActions("GitHub Actions")
    docker = Docker("Docker Image Build")
    registry = ContainerRegistry("ECR Registry")
    helm = Server("Helm Charts")
    eks = GKE("Kubernetes\n(EKS, 3AZ)")
    argocd = ArgoCD("ArgoCD GitOps")
    github >> Edge(label="Builds") >> docker >> Edge(label="Pushes") >> registry
    registry >> Edge(label="Deploys Helm") >> helm >> Edge(label="Deploys on K8s") >> eks
    github >> Edge(label="Pushes manifests") >> argocd >> Edge(label="Reconciles") >> eks

# Failure points
warning_icon = Tempo(Warning\n(Failure)")
[lb, api_gw, kafka, dlq, eks] >> Edge(label="Failure Point") >> warning_icon

Here is a comprehensive system architecture diagram for a global, real-time e-commerce platform showing the full request lifecycle and all your required layers and features:

- Client Layer: Users access via Mobile App (iOS/Android), Web (React SPA), or Smart TV App, hitting global CDN edges in North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific.
- API Gateway: CDN forwards to Load Balancer → API Gateway Cluster, which routes to Auth Service (JWT + OAuth2), Rate Limiter, and a GraphQL Federation Gateway.
- Microservices Layer: Ten domain-driven services (Product Catalog, Inventory, Pricing, User Profile, Cart & Checkout, Order Management, ML Recommendations, Fraud Detection, Notifications, Search [Elasticsearch]). All accessed through GraphQL for synchronous calls.
- Async Communications: Central Kafka Event Bus with key topics (order.created, inventory.updated, fraud.flagged). Includes a dead-letter queue (DLQ) for failed messages, with publishing/subscription edges for each relevant service.
- Data Layer: Each service owns its own datastore (PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra, S3 for images/assets)—polyglot persistence.
- Observability: Prometheus scrapes metrics from all services, Grafana for dashboards. Logs feed to ELK (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana). Jaeger traces distributed requests.
- CI/CD Pipeline: GitHub Actions → Docker image builds → ECR registry → Helm → multi-AZ EKS (Kubernetes), managed by ArgoCD GitOps.
- Failure points are clearly marked.
- Latency annotations and edge type distinctions are included as requested.
